rejectionReason: The workflow's intended outcome is finding and reporting CLI inconsistencies, but its only accepted run artifact is an agent-authored issue. Issue creation, finding counts, command counts, traces, and issue closure do not directly demonstrate that a CLI inconsistency was corrected. The repository has no frozen, machine-verifiable post-run evidence contract that binds a finding to a corrected CLI behavior, so any proposed numeric metric would substitute activity, output volume, or agent judgment for operational attainment.

decisions.selected: Treat the intended outcome as improved CLI consistency and documentation correctness, not inspection activity or issue production.
alternatives: Treat a successful inspection or created issue as attainment
decisions.rationale: The adoption workflow explicitly asks the agent to inspect help output and create a consolidated issue only when findings exist; those are means and outputs rather than correction evidence.

decisions.selected: One CLI consistency audit for the repository state at the run commit.
alternatives: One issue or finding per run
decisions.rationale: The workflow describes a repository-wide audit, while issue and command counts are output and activity dimensions that cannot serve as operational value.

decisions.selected: Bind a run to its repository and commit SHA, retaining the same key for reruns of that subject.
alternatives: Bind a run to the created issue number
Bind a run to the number of findings
decisions.rationale: Repository and commit identity are deterministic from the run subject; safe-output issue creation is optional and therefore cannot be the assignment key.

decisions.selected: Require immutable repository evidence showing that an identified CLI inconsistency was corrected after the audit.
alternatives: Use the safe-output issue body as the outcome
Use evaluator parsing of agent text or traces
decisions.rationale: The workflow freezes help output as an inspection source, but does not define a structured finding identifier, correction link, or accepted post-run repository state. The pre-adoption issue search found adjacent documentation work but no frozen correction protocol.

decisions.selected: No maturation window is frozen because no accepted direct evidence can be collected at its end.
alternatives: Use the issue expiration period as maturation
Use a fixed five-day correction window
decisions.rationale: An issue expiration or elapsed time does not make issue creation or closure evidence of a corrected CLI behavior.

decisions.selected: No primary operational metric; design blocked.
decisions.rationale: Each alternative measures activity, output volume, or an agent-authored classification rather than direct operational attainment, violating the direct-metric requirement.

decisions.selected: No baseline; the design is blocked before a comparable metric exists.
alternatives: Use pre-adoption issue volume as a baseline
Use pre-adoption documentation activity as a baseline
decisions.rationale: Pre-adoption issue and documentation activity are not the same direct operational metric and must not be promoted to a baseline.

decisions.selected: Do not add diagnostics because the available diagnostics are the same prohibited activity and output measures.
decisions.rationale: Keeping those measures separate would not make them operational attainment; the study records the limitation instead.

uncertainties.description: The workflow audits and reports possible defects but does not itself define a machine-verifiable correction outcome.
Run evidence consists of pre-collected help output and optional agent-authored issue text; no structured finding-to-fix evidence is archived.
Repository and run commit identity are deterministic, but they cannot make an unstructured finding-to-fix relationship observable.
Later repository fixes cannot be attributed to this audit without a frozen finding identifier and correction protocol.
